key_insight: SrTiO3-xHx oxyhydrides strongly favor the cis O4H2 anion arrangement, and this ordering is highly sensitive to the choice of DFT+U, requiring HSE06-calibrated energetics for reliable prediction.
engineering_relevance: Accurate anion-order control in perovskite oxyhydrides can guide stability and defect-chemistry tuning for functional energy materials, making calibrated first-principles workflows essential.
method: Built a cluster expansion for SrTiO3-xHx using HSE06-informed training data.
Benchmarked DFT+U mixing and ordering energies against HSE06 to identify U = 3.3 eV as a proxy.
Used ground-state searches and Monte Carlo sampling to probe anion ordering and stability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to ~100 meV/anion variation from different DFT+U choices and a ~200 meV per hydride stabilization for the cis configuration, supported by HSE06 benchmarks, ground states, and Monte Carlo sampling.
watch_item: The ordering conclusions depend strongly on the chosen U value and on transferability of the CE outside the trained configuration set.
paper_title: Long- and Short-Range Anion Order in SrTiO$_{3-x}$H$_x$ Perovskite Oxyhydrides: DFT+$U$ Sensitivity and HSE06 Cluster Expansion
